key_insight: AI rewriting can make radiology text look cleaner while either stripping clinical uncertainty and entities or weakening image-text alignment—the most “standardized” versions are not the most faithful.
clinical_relevance: For multimodal medical AI datasets, documentation style matters: different LLM rewrite tasks can distort the clinical record in ways that may affect training, evaluation, and downstream model behavior.
method: 450 chest X-ray reports from the Indiana University dataset
Generated synthetic rewrites with three LLM tasks: EHR summarization, standardized rewriting, and teaching case preparation
Measured entity erosion, hedging loss, and BiomedCLIP image-text similarity
evidence_signal: EHR summarization caused the largest content loss (51.4% entity erosion, 43.7% hedging loss) but only a 2.5% alignment drop, while standardized rewriting and teaching-case preparation caused smaller content loss yet 14.9–16.5% alignment drops.
watch_item: Rare-pathology degradation was not reliably detectable in this study, so condition-specific monitoring may miss contamination introduced by rewriting style.
paper_title: The Slop Paradox: How Synthetic Standardization Erodes Clinical Uncertainty and Cross-Modal Alignment in AI-Rewritten Radiology Reports
